title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-08-19
content:
Summary:
- Focus this week: kernel optimizations for fused attention, KV-cache memory pressure mitigations, and dynamic batching latency regressions.
- Main outcome: merged two kernel PRs that improve throughput for long-context (8k+) workloads; KV cache eviction tuning rolled to canary; dynamic batching fix shipped to staging with ~10–15% p50 improvement for small requests.

Highlights / Metrics:
- Long-context throughput (8k tokens) improved ~18% steady-state on A100 80GB after fused-attention fixes (PR #342).
- Memory usage for active KV cache entries down ~22% after compacting metadata and switching to single-allocation slab in canary.
- P50 latency for chat small messages (<=32 tokens) in staging moved from 42ms -> 36ms after dynamic-batcher changes; p95 unchanged (still 140–150ms), investigating tail.
- Autoscaling traces: observed a small spike in queue latency when burst traffic hit value-based routing—related to batch formation policy timing.

Kernel Work (Ben + Clara):
- What we did:
  - Fused attention kernel: fixed index-alignment bug that caused extra zero-padding for certain sequence-length modulo values. Tests + microbenchmarks added. (PR: #342)
  - Introduced an alternate GEMM layout path for small head counts; helps 1–2% on short sequences but necessary for compound workloads.
  - Benchmarked multi-stream launches vs single large kernel for 2-stream concurrency; multi-stream wins on occupancy for large batches.
- Outstanding:
  - Need to validate fused kernel on T4/RTX class GPUs (issue: performance varies by warp scheduling). Clara to run tests on T4 grid next week (ticket: INF-4928).

KV Cache (Diego + Emma):
- What we did:
  - Rolled KV compacting to canary: we moved from per-request small allocations to a slab allocator with in-place compaction. Reduces fragmentation and pointer overhead.
  - Introduced adaptive TTL for cached prefixes: frequently-reused prefixes get longer TTL; cold prefixes expire sooner. Initial heuristic based on request frequency over 10m window.
  - Implemented a soft-eviction signal when memory pressure > 75% of reserved KV memory; signal triggers opportunistic compaction during idle cycles.
- Observed behavior:
  - Canary (10% of capacity) showed 22% memory reduction for models with many multi-turn conversations.
  - Saw an edge case where aggressive compaction during high-GPU-util caused slight latency jitter (~5–8ms) — tuned to only compact when GPU utilization < 70%.
- Action items:
  - Diego to open follow-up PR to add instrumentation for per-prefix hit/miss TTL telemetry (INF-4823).
  - Add a TTL override API for debug + customer support.

Batching (Aisha + Clara):
- What we did:
  - Fixed dynamic-batcher grouping bug where very small requests were being batched into large groups causing head-of-line blocking for latency-sensitive requests (fix in PR #346).
  - Tuning: decreased max-wait for latency-sensitive class to 3ms and added probabilistic early-flush when queue depth >= threshold.
  - Introduced a simple fair-queueing layer between priority classes to ensure golden-path low-latency requests are served even under heavy throughput.
- Metrics post-change:
  - Small-message p50 improved 14% in staging; p95 unchanged.
  - Under synthetic mixed load (10% latency class, 90% throughput class) tail latency reduced for latency class by 25%.
- Outstanding:
  - p95 tail still problematic for some multi-tenant mixes. Hypothesis: contention on kernel-level scheduling for certain batch sizes; follow-up to correlate batch sizes with kernel invocation durations.

Incidents / Customer Impact:
- No customer-facing outages. Observed increased latency for one mid-tier customer last Tuesday correlated with cache eviction and a routing policy change; mitigated by temporarily increasing their KV reservation. Root-cause: KV eviction timing + routing spike.

Standup snippets (this week):
- Mon: Kernel fixes landed to feature branch; ran perf sweep on 8k context; noticed mem spike on multi-GPU config.
- Tue: Canary compacting rolled; initial telemetry good; QA found jitter when compaction happens during heavy utilization.
- Wed: Dynamic-batcher regression fix deployed to staging; ran smoke tests with SRE.
- Thu: Correlated tail-latency with batch formation patterns; started trace-level experiments.
- Fri: Sync with SRE + Console team on exposing kv-cache memory per-customer in Console.

Meetings / Decisions:
- 2026-08-18 Kernel deep-dive: decided to prioritize fused-attention stability over additional micro-optimizations for this sprint. Plan to revert some small heuristics that caused T4 regressions.
- KV cache policy sync with Console on 2026-08-19: agreed to expose per-customer KV reservations and a manual override in Console -> feature flagged.

Roadmap / Next week:
- Stabilize fused-attention across GPU families (Ben). Run T4/RTX validation + fix scheduling heuristics (INF-4928).
- Roll TTL telemetry and KV TTL override API to canary (Diego).
- Continue batcher tail debugging: add trace correlation between batch size, kernel runtime, and per-request queue time (Aisha + Clara).
- Add Console telemetry panel prototype for per-customer KV memory and eviction events (Emma + Console PM).

Action items (owner / due):
- Ben: run full kernel matrix tests on T4/RTX and report regressions (due 2026-08-25).
- Clara: complete multi-GPU scheduling experiment and share results in kernel channel (due 2026-08-24).
- Diego: PR for per-prefix TTL telemetry + add alerts for eviction thresholds (INF-4823) (due 2026-08-26).
- Emma: Console prototype for KV metrics + add toggle for override (due 2026-08-28).
- Aisha: correlate staging p95 traces with batch sizes and open follow-up issue (INF-4891) (due 2026-08-23).

Notes / Open questions:
- Is the adaptive TTL heuristic too aggressive for long-running multi-turn chat sessions? Might need an option to pin specific prefixes for certain enterprise customers.
- Consider a per-model KV reservation policy instead of pure per-customer to better handle shared-model multi-tenant scenarios.
- Need clearer SLOs for p95 latency across priority classes; propose to write a short SLO doc next week.

Attachments / links:
- PR #342 (fused-attention fixes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/342
- PR #346 (dynamic-batcher fixes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/346
- Kernel perf confluence page: confluence:Serving Runtime Kernel Perf 2026-08
- Relevant tickets: INF-4823, INF-4891, INF-4928

Quick comments / random notes (notes-to-self style):
- Remember to add a short blurb for product about the KV-memory savings for the next customer check-in.
- Keep canary at 10% for one more week before wider rollout unless telemetry shows regressions.

End of week update.
